name: Burien
seo_title: 5 Christmas Events for Kids in Burien, WA 2026
seo_desc: 5 Christmas events for kids in Burien, WA, 0 free: Santa in the Tin Room and The Nutcracker by Momentum Dance at Highline Performing Arts Center and more.
lede: Burien's Christmas season plays out on the stage of the Highline Performing Arts Center and along SW 152nd Street, where a youth ballet, a family choir concert and a downtown cookie crawl fill the first half of December.
celebrates: Burien does Christmas on stage and on foot. Momentum Dance Academy and Ensemble dances The Nutcracker at the Highline Performing Arts Center with support from the City of Burien, Arts WA and 4Culture, and Northwest Associated Arts follows with ChristmasSounds, which it calls Burien's favorite holiday tradition, with choirs from KidSounds to SilverSounds. Downtown, Discover Burien sends families out on a Holiday Cookie Crawl to collect treats from local businesses. The Highline Heritage Museum on SW 152nd Street holds an annual La Posada celebration of Mexican holiday traditions, and Santa visits Olde Burien for photo days that double as a food drive.
lastyear: In 2025 the Highline Heritage Museum held its annual La Posada celebration on Saturday, December 13, from 5 to 8 pm at 819 SW 152nd Street. The museum invited people of all ages and backgrounds to a lively evening immersed in the holiday traditions of Mexico, designed to build cultural understanding and community connection. Discover Burien's Holiday Cookie Crawl and the Momentum Nutcracker at the Highline Performing Arts Center are also returning December traditions downtown.
facts: Burien takes its name from Lake Burien, a 44 acre kettle lake left by a melting chunk of glacier. The lake was named for Gottlieb and Emma Burian, settlers from Lower Silesia who bought a 120 acre homestead at its southeast corner in 1889. Nobody recorded how the a in Burian became an e. The city incorporated on February 28, 1993, after voters chose the name Burien over earlier proposals such as Highline.
trains: Burien once had its own electric railway. Starting in 1912, a streetcar line backed by local landowners ran from Riverside through White Center to Lake Burien and Seahurst. Through service to Seattle began in 1919, was suspended in 1929, and the line was shut down in 1931. Today the nearest trains are Link light rail at Tukwila International Boulevard and SeaTac/Airport stations, and Sounder and Amtrak Cascades at Tukwila Station. For a holiday train ride, the Northwest Railway Museum in Snoqualmie runs the North Pole Limited.

Santa Claus Is Coming To B-Town
Santa visits the Tin Room in Olde Burien for photo days paired with a food drive for the Highline Area Food Bank.
kidfact: Burien was named after a lake, and the lake was named after a family called Burian. Somewhere along the way the a turned into an e, and nobody wrote down why.
faq: Is there a Nutcracker in Burien?

Yes. Momentum Dance Academy and Ensemble performs The Nutcracker each December at the Highline Performing Arts Center, 401 South 152nd Street. The full length ballet features the Momentum Ballet Ensemble and academy dancers, and the company lists separate prices for adults, seniors and students, with lap children under 2 free.

ChristmasSounds is a holiday choir concert by Northwest Associated Arts at the Highline Performing Arts Center. Its ensembles ChoralSounds, SilverSounds, TeenSounds and KidSounds sing traditional carols and contemporary favorites. Youth 17 and under get in free with a paying adult, and tickets are sold online or at the door.
What is the Burien Holiday Cookie Crawl?

It is a Discover Burien event where ticket holders start at the Discover Burien office, 611 SW 152nd Street, pick up a map and a reusable bag, then stroll downtown collecting holiday treats at participating businesses. Tickets are limited to 100 and the organizer calls it suitable for all ages.
Where is the Highline Heritage Museum?

The Highline Heritage Museum is at 819 SW 152nd Street in downtown Burien. It hosts an annual La Posada celebration in December that shares the holiday traditions of Mexico with people of all ages and backgrounds. Check the museum's events calendar for the current year's date.
